diagnostic: Stage B evaluation candidate: completed-output fission forensics
scope: 32 candidate worlds, seeds 18000 through 18031, 120 days; no baseline read, acceptance verdict, tuning, simulation or branch replay.

terminal_gate.runlog_hash_omitted_reason: RUNLOG also records the still-running baseline arm and is mutable; candidate-specific exit file and summary are hashed.

inferences: The retained elder exclusion explains all 18 split couples: the adult and every eligible member of that household depart while the elder is ineligible.
Individual group_min top-up is ruled out in all 24 departures: final selected sizes 10–14 exceed group_min 6; the terminal top-up branch would stop at 6.
Every selected eligible household block is whole. No observed split requires individual top-up.

For all 24 departures the integer 35-percent reconstruction from the observed living parent partition, rounded half-up and clamped 6–14, equals the selected size. Actual runtime k is not directly recorded.
unobservable: No branch-entry markers or ordered seeding/filling rank decisions are recorded. Exclusion/top-up interpretation is a source-supported inference, not direct branch telemetry.
Runtime settlement roster count and local k are not stored in departure events; integer target-size arithmetic is explicitly conditional on observed living partition size matching the roster count.
Lifetime summaries record aggregate adult exposure rather than exact elder-transition ticks. Hourly observations bracket transitions and directly establish stage at departure.
No counterfactual elder policy or later acceptance outcome is inferred. Baseline and evaluator files were not read or changed.
